task_instance: Write a production Apache Airflow DAG for a daily incremental sales ETL pipeline (extract a date-partitioned CSV, transform, load to parquet) using the skill's patterns: TaskFlow API, retries with exponential backoff, per-task execution timeout, idempotent processing keyed on the logical date ({{ ds }}), a failure-alert callback, and an always-run cleanup task; plus a matching pytest/DagBag test file (Pattern 6).
task_instance_note: The skill's core deliverable is authoring production DAG code following documented best practices, which is a pure text-authoring task.
outcome_detail: Produced dags/daily_sales_etl.py and tests/test_dags.py as text files following the skill's SKILL.md Quick Start and references/details.md (TaskFlow API pattern 1, error-handling pattern 5, testing pattern 6). Verified the DAG by inspection against every Do/Don't in SKILL.md: uses TaskFlow API; sets execution_timeout; idempotent/incremental via {{ ds }} partition paths (no now()-derived keys in the written partition); retries=3 with retry_exponential_backoff and max_retry_delay; catchup=False with a comment on implications; depends_on_past=False; no global state (pandas imported lazily inside each task, heavy logic not at parse time); cleanup task uses ALL_DONE trigger rule, end uses NONE_FAILED_MIN_ONE_SUCCESS; failure callback wired via default_args. Dependency graph is acyclic (linear extract>transform>load>notify fan-out to cleanup/end). The companion test file encodes structural assertions (no import errors, task set, retries, no cycles, trigger rule).
verification_limitation: Executing the provided DagBag/pytest tests to confirm the DAG parses inside a real Airflow install was not possible in this runtime (no code execution, Airflow/pytest not runnable). Verification was done by code review against the skill's checklist instead of by running the tests. This is a limit on runtime-level verification, not on producing the core deliverable, which is DAG source code.
